MGT 409 · Final project · October 26, 2026

Mian Capital

A values-aware investing research assistant and portfolio evidence view for people who want their financial choices to reflect Islamic principles.

Student: Wali Mian · Yale School of Management

GitHub: https://github.com/wali-mian1/mian-capital

Live app: No public deployment yet. Local demo: http://127.0.0.1:8050.

Figure 1. Current standalone Dash website, captured October 26, 2026.

The prototype combines an agent with real market and web tools, a deterministic portfolio evidence calculation, and a paper-money learning lab. The old external front end is not integrated because its source was unavailable during this build. This report describes the current working app and its evidence limits.

Mian Capital · Wali Mian1 / 11
01 / Motivation

A specific gap in an important decision

A faith-conscious investor often has to answer two questions at once: “What does this investment do?” and “Does it fit my constraints?”

The user

Community members who avoid activities such as alcohol and gambling and want an understandable starting point for Shariah-oriented investing. A second user is a newly high-earning professional who has not yet opened a brokerage account. The home page links to a separate Learn page with short account explanations.

Current workflow

Search a fund name, find its ticker, open a price page, locate the issuer's screening statement, check recent news, and manually compare holdings. Many sources mix strategy claims with investment marketing.

Where time and trust are lost

Names and tickers are easy to confuse; a name passed to a market-data API can return nothing. A fund's Islamic label also does not establish that every current underlying holding passes one chosen screening method. Different screens may use different sector and financial-ratio thresholds. A single unexplained “compliant” badge hides those distinctions.

Mian Capital gives one place to ask a research question, inspect a readable summary of the tool request and result, see dated source links, and put a simple portfolio into an evidence view. It deliberately keeps unknown positions visible. The account setup page addresses a separate first step: explaining brokerage choices and mechanics while the visitor keeps control of credentials and trades.

Figure 2. Founder bio and brokerage education flow.

Why this is a real need: The founder studied mathematics and actuarial science at UT Austin and spent four years working on retirement and benefits as an actuary. That experience informs the problem framing; this project does not claim a measured market size or a verified financial return for users.

02 / Novelty

Where the app fits among existing products

Zoya and Musaffa already offer Islamic investing research and screening tools. Wahed offers Shariah-oriented investment products. These are meaningful comparators, not empty stand-ins. Mian.io is Mian Capital's free, in-house research chat. It ties a source-backed conversation to account education and a portfolio screen that opens each fund and checks the companies inside it. It uses only recent browser-session questions for follow-ups; it does not build a persistent investor profile.

What is new here

  1. Inspectable agent steps: The chat offers a collapsed plain-language summary of each successful price or search step; the report preserves the detailed tool trace. Price calls now render dated charts; five quick prompts submit common questions. “Amana Growth Fund” resolves to AMAGX before the tool runs.
  2. Look inside the fund, not just its label: Portfolio Screening pulls each fund's top ten holdings and shows, company by company and in the user's own dollars, whether any holding touches alcohol, gambling, tobacco, weapons, fossil fuels, or high debt. A label like “Shariah ETF” becomes a list of companies the user can see.
  3. Learning before action: A separate Learn page uses short cards to explain brokerage accounts, 401(k)s, Traditional IRAs, Roth IRAs, and common investment products with Investor.gov and IRS links. A front-page $100/month illustration states its assumed 6% return; Paper Lab separately labels historical data and user-assumed future growth.

03 / Agent design

Two bounded agents; deterministic calculators

Mian.io is the free visitor research chat; its PydanticAI agent answers questions using the current browser-session conversation for follow-ups. The model is gpt-6-luna, called through OpenAI's Responses API with OPENAI_API_KEY. Earlier development runs were routed through Portkey until that key's allowance ran out. It selects between exactly two capabilities. A second holdings screening agent, also gpt-6-luna, classifies companies inside the user's funds. Dollar math, debt ratios, and paper-money scenarios are Python functions outside the model so their numbers are repeatable.

Price tool

get_stock_price(ticker,start,stop) accepts one of 12 supported tickers, validates dates and an exclusive stop date, and returns dated Yahoo closes and a source URL. Name aliases resolve before the call.

Web search

OpenAI native web_search handles recent news and current issuer claims. The app exposes returned URLs; external pages are treated as untrusted data.

Holdings screening agent

Takes up to 20 funds or stocks, fetches each fund's top ten holdings and each company's sector, industry, description, debt, and market value from Yahoo. The agent returns a typed result per company: clear, flag, or unclear for alcohol, gambling, tobacco, weapons, and fossil fuels, plus a one-line reason. Debt over 30% of market value is computed in Python, not by the model. Classifications are cached, so a repeat screen makes no model call. Paper Lab uses yfinance history and a compounding formula. Nothing can place orders or access a brokerage.

Run limits: 4 model requests, 4 tool calls, 2,000 total output tokens, and an 850-token response setting. Chat history is capped at six recent turns and 400 characters each. The price universe and date span are bounded in code.

The two agents do not hand off to each other: each has one job and its own limits. Splitting them keeps the screening agent's input to company data only, so web text and chat history cannot steer a compliance flag.

04 / Tokenomics

Measured tokens, stated assumptions

The two observed runs recorded API token usage in the project evidence log; token counters are not shown in the visitor chat. The calculations below use OpenAI's published gpt-6-luna standard rates on October 25, 2026: $0.10 per million uncached input tokens, $0.01 per million cached input tokens, $0.50 per million output tokens. Native web search is $10 per 1,000 calls, plus search-content tokens billed at model rates. The model usage count is taken as already including content tokens reported by the API; the web call fee is added separately. Portkey or account-specific charges are unknown.

Observed runInputCachedOutputWeb callsEstimated total
AMAGX price10,2449,7221170$0.000208
HLAL news14,5324,8625163$0.031274
Portfolio screen (15 companies)2,28809500$0.000704
Price run formula: (10,244 − 9,722) × $0.10 / 1,000,000 + 9,722 × $0.01 / 1,000,000 + 117 × $0.50 / 1,000,000 = $0.00020792.
News run formula: (14,532 − 4,862) × $0.10 / 1,000,000 + 4,862 × $0.01 / 1,000,000 + 516 × $0.50 / 1,000,000 + 3 × $0.01 = $0.03127362.

Interpretation

Web search dominates the observed news cost: $0.03 of approximately $0.0313. The observed three-search behavior may be more than needed for a simple news question. Caching reduced the input-token portion of the price run substantially; it does not eliminate the hosted web-tool fee.

Pricing source: OpenAI API pricing, fetched October 25, 2026. These are estimates at published standard rates, not an invoice. Prices and account routing may change.

04 / Scale and savings

The economics depend on search frequency

Scenario: one user asks 20 research questions per month, half price requests and half news requests. Each type is assumed to cost exactly what the observed example cost. This is a planning assumption, not measured usage across a user population.

Volume10 price + 10 news / userEstimated monthly API + web fee
1 user20 turns$0.3148
100 users2,000 turns$31.48
10,000 users200,000 turns$3,148.15

A concrete savings lever

Reducing the observed news run from three web searches to one would save approximately $0.02 per news turn before any change in token usage. At 10 news turns per user each month, that is about $0.20 per user, $20 per 100 users, or $2,000 per 10,000 users monthly. It might also miss corroborating sources; quality should be checked before imposing the tighter limit. The app currently permits up to four total tool calls, so this saving is a proposal, not an achieved result.

Other costs and limits

  • Yahoo Finance/yfinance prices have no separately measured API charge in this prototype, but availability and licensing for scaled commercial use need review.
  • Hosting, monitoring, human advisor time, payment processing, taxes, and any Portkey markup are excluded.
  • The reported token totals came from two sample questions. They should not be treated as a stable distribution without more logs.
  • A first portfolio screen of 15 companies cost about $0.0007; cached companies cost nothing on later screens. Even one fresh screen per user per month adds only about $7 at 10,000 users. Paper Lab makes no model call.
Measured cost-quality tradeoff: For HLAL over 2025-10-27 to 2026-10-26, the tool received 250 daily closes but sent only the first and last 12 to the model: 1,057 JSON bytes instead of 11,033. This trims the tool payload by about 90%, but omitted the 2026-04-28 close. A separate narrow query recovered that quote ($65.76), adding a tool call. The ticker and one-year limits also reduce breadth.

05 / Safety

Guardrails and a blocked attack

The app handles financial questions and untrusted web results. Plausible failures include a fabricated price, a wrong ticker, a false compliance claim, a prompt injection in search content, leakage of the Portkey key, and an unbounded number of paid tool calls.

RiskImplemented controlRemaining risk
Wrong or invented pricePrice claims must use the yfinance tool; output includes date and source. Ticker is validated against ten Shariah-oriented research funds and two market comparison ETFs.Yahoo prices may be delayed or unavailable.
False religious rulingSystem instruction distinguishes issuer claim from independent verification. Portfolio shows unknown weight.Issuer strategy does not verify current constituents or ratios.
Secret requestPre-model guard blocks requests to reveal keys, .env, or hidden instructions.Pattern matching will not catch every paraphrase.
Wrong debt flagDebt ratio is computed in code. A test flagged TSMC at 37% because Yahoo reports its debt in Taiwan dollars and market value in US dollars; the screen now shows “?” when currencies differ.Ratios use current market value, not a 36-month average.
Runaway spendRequest, tool-call, output-token, range, and ticker limits.Three web searches were still used in one ordinary news run.

Figure 6. Actual attempt to reveal PORTKEY_API_KEY was blocked before a model call; measured token usage was zero.

Evidence: The browser displayed the refusal and a safety_guard · blocked event. The local audit line recorded the reason without a key or raw chat text. External prompt-injection handling is instructed, but a separate hostile-page test is still needed.

Faster answers for a real user

A Mian Capital user tried the app and agreed to let us share their experience. Their account is paraphrased below; the timings are their own estimates, not a lab measurement.

What our user told us

They tapped SPUS vs SPY and had both funds' prices and charts in about 20 seconds; on the web it would have taken closer to a minute, with two tabs. They then asked Mian.io for insights on the two funds and got an objective comparison of the tickers, which they called very useful. Earlier, they compared HLAL and SPUS, used Paper Lab to replay a trade they had considered a month before but never placed, felt more confident about it, and then asked us for help opening a brokerage account.

07 / Limits and next steps

What the evidence cannot yet support

  1. Screening depth: The portfolio screen covers each fund's top ten holdings (about 58–60% of HLAL, SPUS, and AMAGX), not every company. It does not check interest income or compute purification. The AI classification can be wrong; each flag shows its reason so the user can check it.
  2. Methodology choice: Shariah screens differ. A future release should show the selected authority or index standard, exact thresholds, date, and any conflicting conclusion.
  3. Security breadth: The agent prices ten Shariah-oriented or Amana funds and two broad-market comparison ETFs. SPY and QQQ carry no Shariah-screening claim. Unsupported stocks and ambiguous names need explicit review; broad stock screening would require vetted fundamentals and business-activity data.
  4. News quality: Search result URLs are surfaced, but not every third-party statement has been independently corroborated. Prefer official issuer and regulator documents for consequential claims.
  5. Client workflow: The About page offers account setup education only. There is no account connection, personalized trade recommendation, credential collection, or order execution.
  6. Deployment and evidence: An October 26 fresh clone installed dependencies, found a dummy parent-folder .env, and returned HTTP 200 for all six then-current routes in about 25 seconds of command runtime. The Testimonials route passed desktop and mobile browser checks. More timed user comparisons and verbatim quotes remain.

Figure 7. Full-width historical paper chart; the future mode separately uses a user-supplied rate, not a forecast.

Priority: Screen every holding, not just the top ten, using a full-holdings data feed and a user-selected methodology (AAOIFI or S&P). Then time more users on real tasks.

Reproduce the prototype

From the repository root, create .venv, install requirements.txt, put OPENAI_API_KEY in a root or parent-folder .env, run .venv/bin/python app.py, and open http://127.0.0.1:8050. The README gives exact steps. The included portfolio.json is illustrative; no real client holdings or keys are included.

Evidence inventory

output/CHATBOT_EVIDENCE.md records the observed tool traces, counts, browser checks, and screenshot filenames. The HTML report embeds its screenshots directly, so the file opens without a separate assets folder. The application itself needs its Python dependencies and internet access for live price and search calls.

The GitHub repository is public. The Testimonials tab distinguishes a permissioned anonymous paraphrase of founder-reported tester feedback from illustrative examples. No timed saving or financial outcome is claimed.
